title: Turn any website into a spreadsheet
description: Extract directories, listings, products, and profiles into clean rows and columns, with a sample first and a source link on every row.
introduction: Copying a directory or a product catalog into a spreadsheet is the kind of job that eats an afternoon. Most AI tools don't help much, because they read pages the way a person does: one screen at a time.

Strawberry's agent is built for the web. Many sites load their data through their own requests in the background, and Strawberry can read those directly. A job that takes an hour in a tool that wasn't made for the web often takes a minute here, and thousands of rows stay cheap.

blocks.text: Anything that repeats on a website and belongs in rows:

items: Every clinic, agency, or supplier listed in a directory for a city or region
A product catalog with prices, variants, and stock status
Speakers, exhibitors, or sponsors from a conference site
Job listings, property listings, or public records
Profiles on a marketplace or community site

items.context: Point Strawberry at a site, say which fields you need, and get a checked sample before the full run.

items: Say what each row is, which fields you need, and roughly how many rows.
If the data is going into an existing sheet, Strawberry reads its columns first so everything lines up.
You get 10 to 20 rows to check. At high volume, a small mistake repeats thousands of times, so this is where it gets caught.
The full run covers the whole site: every page, infinite scroll, load-more buttons, and detail pages.
The result lands in a spreadsheet, with a link to the source on every row.

blocks.text: A value that wasn't found stays marked as not found. It never becomes a guess, and it never quietly turns into a "no". If a site blocks access or asks for a login, Strawberry stops and hands it back to you rather than working around it.

Once a run works, save it as a skill so the next extraction starts from the same fields and checks. If the data changes over time, like prices, listings, or openings, a Routine can rerun it on a schedule and tell you only what changed.
